found.domain: Diablo 2 Resurrected ethereal items (mature ladder economy)

items.name: Ethereal Sandstorm Trek
items.category: Unique boots (Scarabshell Boots) - Pillar 1 hidden value / self-repair
items.rarityTier: Uncommon perfect roll
items.whyValuable: This is the textbook case of ethereal being a pure upside with no downside. Sandstorm Trek has the self-repair mod Repairs 1 Durability in 20 Seconds, so the ethereal version quietly heals its own durability and never breaks, while gaining the ethereal +50% defense on top of its already high +140-170% enhanced defense. A player wearing them (not just a merc) gets a permanent, unbreakable boot with insane defense plus big strength and vitality. Casual players think all eth armor eventually dies. These do not.
items.teachingPoint: Self-repair mod plus ethereal equals a free permanent defense boost. The 20-second repair timer outpaces normal durability loss, so the boots effectively never break even on your own character, not just a mercenary.
items.quality: Perfect eth roll wants 15 str / 15 vita / high ED / 70 poison res
factClaims: Sandstorm Trek is a unique Scarabshell Boots
It has the mod Repairs 1 Durability In 20 Seconds (self-repair)
Base stats include +20% Faster Run/Walk, +20% Faster Hit Recovery, +140-170% Enhanced Defense when ethereal, +10-15 Strength, +10-15 Vitality, 50% Slower Stamina Drain, +40-70% Poison Resist
Ethereal grants roughly +50% defense over the non-ethereal version
Because of self-repair, the ethereal version is strictly superior to non-ethereal even when worn by the player character

items.name: Ethereal Superior Thresher / Giant Thresher (for Infinity or Insight)
items.alias: eth thresher, eth GT, 4os/5os/6os eth thresher
items.category: White/superior polearm base - Pillar 1 hidden value (base, not item)
items.rarityTier: Perfect superior eth with max sockets is rare
items.whyValuable: A plain white polearm can be worth a fortune. The value is entirely in the base being ethereal, superior (+ enhanced damage on a white item), and hitting max sockets from Larzuk. Threshers have the fastest effective attack speed among high-damage polearms, so an eth superior Thresher becomes the best base for Insight (merc mana/damage) and Infinity (Conviction aura). Mercs never lose durability, so ethereal is free +50% damage with zero downside. A perfect eth superior 4-socket Thresher is one of the most coveted white bases in the game.
items.teachingPoint: For merc polearm runewords the ideal base is ethereal AND superior (a white item that rolled bonus enhanced damage) AND max sockets. Larzuk gives a Thresher 5 sockets and a Giant Thresher 6, but Insight needs exactly 4 and Infinity needs 4, so you want a base that dropped with the right socket count or you cube/Larzuk carefully.
items.quality: Perfect = ethereal + superior with high % ED + correct socket count
factClaims: Thresher requires level 53, 152 strength, 118 dexterity and can roll up to 5 sockets (Larzuk gives 5)
Giant Thresher can roll up to 6 sockets (Larzuk gives 6)
Insight is a 4-socket runeword and Infinity is a 4-socket runeword
Mercenaries do not lose durability, so an ethereal merc weapon never degrades
Threshers are favored for Insight/Infinity due to high attack speed relative to damage

items.name: Ethereal Breath of the Dying Berserker Axe (eBotD)
items.category: Runeword weapon - Pillar 1 / historic best-in-slot melee
items.rarityTier: Very rare (needs eth base + Zod/Ber... plus Vex/Hel/Eld/Zod/Eth/Ort)
items.whyValuable: Breath of the Dying contains a Zod rune, which grants Indestructible. Indestructible completely cancels the ethereal durability problem, so an ethereal BotD keeps its +50% damage forever and literally cannot break. On a Berserker Axe (highest DPS one-hander) this is the single hardest-hitting one-handed weapon in the game. The eth version is dramatically better than non-eth purely because Zod removes the only downside.
items.teachingPoint: Zod = Indestructible, and Indestructible overrides ethereal degradation. That is why the only ethereal weapons safe to swing on your own character forever are ones with a Zod rune or a naturally indestructible/self-repair source. eBotD is the poster child.
items.quality: Perfect eBotD wants near-max enhanced damage (roll ~355-415%) on an eth zerker axe
factClaims: Breath of the Dying is the runeword Vex Hel El Eld Zod Eth (6 sockets)
It requires a Zod rune, which grants the Indestructible property

items.name: Ethereal Titan's Revenge
items.category: Unique throwing/melee javelin (Ceremonial Javelin) - Pillar 1 hidden value (replenish quantity)
items.rarityTier: Uncommon-rare perfect eth
items.whyValuable: Throwing weapons normally seem terrible ethereal because you deplete the stack and cannot repair/refill it. Titan's Revenge dodges this entirely because it has Replenishes Quantity: the stack regenerates over time. So an ethereal Titan's gets the +50% damage boost while its ammo just grows back. It is the go-to ethereal throwing weapon and a favorite melee/throw Javazon weapon, adding +2 skills, dex, str, run/walk and life leech.
items.teachingPoint: Replenishes Quantity is the throwing-weapon equivalent of self-repair. It is why an ethereal Titan's Revenge is desirable while most ethereal throwing weapons are junk. The quantity regenerates faster than reasonable use depletes it.
items.quality: Perfect eth Titan's wants max ED (~150-184%) and high life leech

items.name: The Ethereal Socketing Bug (eth-bugged armor) - REMOVED in D2R
items.rarityTier: N/A (does not exist in D2R)
items.whyValuable: Historically enormous. In classic LoD, using the Cube socket recipe on an ethereal armor applied the +50% ethereal defense bonus a SECOND time, producing double-boosted defense (100 def base could become 150 with sockets, and the effect stacked). Eth-bugged armors were prized trophies. Blizzard removed this in D2R (fixed by early-access beta), so those legendary sky-high defense numbers are no longer obtainable. The item to feature is the myth itself and why D2R defense values look lower than old screenshots.
items.teachingPoint: The eth socket bug is DEAD in D2R. Applying the cube socket recipe to an ethereal armor in D2R gives sockets but NOT a second +50% defense boost. If someone quotes classic-era eth-bugged defense numbers, they do not apply to modern D2R ladder.
items.history: In pre-D2R versions the socketing recipes double-applied the ethereal +50% defense bonus, creating 'eth-bugged' armors with abnormally high defense. Blizzard removed this exploit in D2R, standardizing defense across all socketing methods.
items.quality: N/A

items.name: The Zod / Ethereal Indestructible Rule (and the old Zod-eth bug)
items.rarityTier: N/A (mechanic)
items.whyValuable: This rule is WHY ethereal runewords like eBotD and eth Death exist as top-tier items. Zod grants Indestructible, which cancels ethereal durability loss, so an eth item with Zod keeps +50% damage forever. Historically there was also a Zod-eth BUG in v1.09: socketing Zod into an ethereal item that had BONUS durability would drop it to 0 and ruin it, while Zod in an eth item with NO bonus durability made it correctly indestructible. That bug was fixed in v1.10 and is not present in D2R.
items.teachingPoint: Zod = Indestructible = the clean fix for ethereal degradation. In old versions Zod on certain ethereal bases (ones with +durability, like Messerschmidt's Reaver with +25 dura) could brick the item; this was patched out by v1.10 and does not affect D2R.

items.name: Bases that CANNOT be ethereal (Phase Blade and indestructible bases)
items.category: Reference / Pillar 2 historic significance (why some grails have no eth version)
items.rarityTier: N/A (reference)
items.whyValuable: A crucial gotcha for traders. Phase Blades have no durability and are naturally indestructible, so they cannot spawn ethereal in any quality. That means there is NO such thing as an ethereal Grief Phase Blade or eth Phase Blade CTA, no matter what a listing claims. Same logic for other naturally indestructible bases. Set items also cannot be ethereal. Knowing which grails simply have no ethereal version prevents getting scammed and explains why some best-in-slot weapons never get an eth premium.
items.teachingPoint: Phase Blade cannot be ethereal (it is natively indestructible with no durability). Any 'ethereal Phase Blade' offer is fake. Set items also never spawn ethereal.

found.notes:
Economy baseline assumed: mature D2R ladder. No prices given; tiers are openly guesses. Key mechanic facts that gate everything: (1) Ethereal grants ~+50% defense (armor) or ~+50% damage (weapons) but halves durability and cannot be repaired at vendor or cube. (2) Ethereal is a pure upside in three cases only: on a mercenary (mercs never lose durability), on items with self-repair mods (Sandstorm Trek 20s, Skullder's Ire 5s, Hone Sundan 10s, Skin of the Flayed One 10s), or on items with Indestructible/Zod (eBotD, eth Death). (3) Throwing weapons are the exception-to-the-exception: Replenishes Quantity (Titan's Revenge) makes eth throwing viable by regenerating the stack.

Verification caveats worth flagging before publishing any single item:
- Sandstorm Trek base = Scarabshell Boots, req level 64, self-repair 20s: CONFIRMED across diablo2.io + fandom + gamerguides.
- Thresher sockets (5 max, Larzuk 5) and Giant Thresher (6 max, Larzuk 6): CONFIRMED diablo2.io base pages. Double-check the exact socket count a given runeword needs vs what the base dropped with; Insight and Infinity are both 4-socket.
- eth socket bug removed in D2R: CONFIRMED (Blizzard forums + diablo2.io + lilura). Strong Pillar 2 pick.
- Zod-eth v1.09 bug fixed v1.10: from fandom/diablowiki; solid but consider a second source before making it the headline claim of a post.
- Phase Blade cannot be eth: CONFIRMED. Good anti-scam teaching item.
- Skin of the Flayed One repairs 1 dura/10s and Skullder's Ire 1 dura/5s: sourced but I did not independently confirm every second on diablo2.io; verify the exact repair interval per item before printing it as a factClaim, since players will catch a wrong number.
- I did NOT get exact enhanced-defense ranges verified for every armor from a primary source (some came from vendor/blog pages). Re-verify ED% ranges, str reqs, and req levels on diablo2.io or the Arreat Summit before publishing any specific number. diablo2.io and fandom both returned 403/402 to WebFetch during research, so stats here lean on WebSearch summaries of those same pages plus lilura1 blog and vendor listings; treat exact numeric ranges as needing one more primary-source pass.

Deliberately AVOIDED as too obvious/boring per the selection bar: plain eth Infinity showcase, eth CoH, eth Fortitude as a headline (kept only as a base-value teaching example). The strongest 'wait, THAT?' picks here are eth Sandstorm Trek (self-repair makes eth strictly better on your own char), eth Titan's Revenge (replenish quantity), eth Hone Sundan (self-repair + crushing blow), eth Bonehew (deep cut), and the two historic mechanic entries (eth socket bug removed, Zod rule + old bug).

Also the repair rate: Skullder's is Repairs 1 Durability In 5 Seconds — the finding states this correctly. Fix the MF-at-99 number to ~123%. Otherwise unique Russet Armor, +1 all skills, +160-200% ED, self-repair-safe-when-worn all confirmed. Keep after correcting MF value.

checked.name: Ethereal Bonehew (Ogre Axe)
checked.corrections: FABRICATED STAT: the finding claims 'bonus poison damage' — Bonehew has NO poison damage. Its actual mods are +270-320% ED, Level 14 Corpse Explosion (30 charges), Prevent Monster Heal, 30% IAS, 50% Chance To Cast Level 16 Bone Spear On Striking, Socketed (2), req level 64. The Corpse Explosion charges (Lvl 14, 30 charges) and 2 sockets and eth-merc use are correct. Remove the poison-damage claim and optionally add the CtC Bone Spear and Prevent Monster Heal. Keep after correction; genuinely obscure Pillar 1 item.

checked.name: Ethereal Shaftstop / eth merc body armor
checked.corrections: Core Shaftstop mods confirmed: Physical Damage Reduced by 30%, +250 Defense vs Missiles, +60 Life (note it is 'Defense vs Missiles' = +250, and finding said +250 — correct). Ethereal +50% base defense compounding with %ED is correct mechanically. However the base-defense figures are OFF: Shaftstop's non-eth total defense is 599-684 (unique Mesh Armor), not '~297-320' as the finding states — 297-320 is not a Shaftstop value. The eth total will be higher than 599-684 (roughly 800-1000+ with the eth base bonus compounding), so the '830-1000+' eth figure is in a plausible ballpark but the '297-320 base' baseline is wrong. Sacred Armor being the highest-base-defense body armor favored for eth Fortitude is correct. Fix the base-defense numbers. Keep.

checked.name: The Ethereal Socketing Bug (eth-bug / ebug) — removed in D2R
checked.corrections: DOCUMENTED FACT, not folklore. In classic LoD the cube add-sockets recipe erroneously applied the ethereal +50% defense bonus a second time (to total, not base defense), producing 'eth-bugged' armor. Fixed in D2R (as of early-access beta) via 'defense parity' so cube/Larzuk/natural sockets all yield identical defense. Strong Pillar 2 historic fit and genuinely surprising.

checked.name: The Zod / Indestructible Rule and the v1.09 Zod-eth bug
checked.corrections: DOCUMENTED FACT. Zod grants Indestructible, which cancels ethereal durability loss. In v1.09 and earlier, socketing Zod into an ethereal item that had BONUS durability dropped it to 0 (ruined it), while Zod into an eth item without bonus durability correctly made it indestructible. Fixed in v1.10; not present in D2R. Ethereal items cannot be repaired by vendor or cube — confirmed. Good Pillar 2 fit.

checked.name: Bases that CANNOT be ethereal (Phase Blade, indestructible bases, set items)
checked.corrections: Phase Blades have no durability and cannot spawn ethereal in any quality — confirmed (so no eth Grief/CTA Phase Blade). Set items never spawn ethereal — confirmed. Naturally-indestructible / no-durability bases and items with the indestructible affix do not spawn ethereal — confirmed. The Ginther's Rift nuance is correct: it is a unique Dimensional Blade that upgrades to a Phase Blade base; an ethereal Ginther's Rift stays ethereal after the upgrade, so an 'ethereal Phase Blade' exists only via that upgrade path, not as a natural drop. Strong anti-scam Pillar 2 reference.

verify.notes:
Adversarial fact-check complete against Arreat Summit-equivalent sources (diablo2.io, Fandom/diablowiki, PureDiablo, maxroll, d2runewizard, lootcube). Verified runeword recipes rune-by-rune, socket counts, base stats, req levels, variable stat ranges, and both historical bug mechanics.

CONCRETE CORRECTIONS (checkable errors players would catch):
1. Skullder's Ire (#10): '+81.25% MF at level 99' is WRONG. It is 1.25% per level = ~123% at level 99. The finding's own '1.25 per level' contradicts its 81.25 figure.
2. Bonehew (#11): 'bonus poison damage' is FABRICATED. Bonehew has no poison damage; it has 50% CtC Bone Spear on striking and Prevent Monster Heal instead.
3. Shaftstop (#12): base defense '~297-320' is WRONG. Shaftstop non-eth total defense is 599-684. The eth '830-1000+' target is plausible but the stated baseline is not a Shaftstop number.
4. Titan's Revenge (#5): incomplete — it has BOTH +2 Amazon Skill Levels AND +2 Javelin/Spear Skills; finding lists only the latter.
5. Reaper's Toll (#6): imprecise — Decrepify slows and increases physical damage taken; describing it as reducing 'defense and physical resistance' conflates it with Amplify Damage. Also precise values are 33% CtC Lvl 1 Decrepify, +33% Deadly Strike, 11-15% life steal, Ignore Target's Defense.

VERIFIED CORRECT (no change): #1 Sandstorm Trek (minor wording nit only), #2 Threshers (all sockets/reqs exact), #3 eBotD (recipe exact), #4 Tomb Reaver, #7 Andariel's, #8 Vampire Gaze, #9 Hone Sundan (91-str eth math is correct), #13 eth-bug (documented), #14 Zod-eth bug (documented), #15 Phase Blade/set/Ginther's (all correct incl. the upgrade nuance).

SELECTION BAR: I recommend keeping all 15. None are the banned obvious items (Enigma/Shako/Ber/Griffon's/Infinity). eBotD (#3) and eth Andariel's (#7) are the closest to common knowledge, but their VALUE-CARRYING angle here is the ethereal/Zod-durability interaction and the merc-only gotcha, which fits the hidden-value pillar, so they clear the bar. All historical items (#13/#14/#15) are documented fact rather than folklore and are strong Pillar 2 fits. No item traced only to forum hearsay; both bug claims are corroborated by multiple sources including Blizzard forums.

found.domain: Diablo 2 Resurrected rare items: circlets, jewelry, gloves, boots, jewels hitting exact valuable affix combinations (mature ladder economy)

items.name: Rare 2/20 Sorceress Circlet (+2 Sorceress Skills / 20% FCR)
items.alias: "2/20 sorc circ", "Arch-Angel's Circlet of the Magus"
items.rarityTier: Extremely rare to roll; among the most demanded rare rolls in the game
items.whyValuable: A rare circlet is the ONLY caster helm that can stack +2 to a class's skills AND 20% Faster Cast Rate AND a socket AND life/resist/stats all at once. Shako gives +2 all skills but no FCR and no free suffix slots; a 2/20 circlet lets a sorc hit an FCR breakpoint from the helm slot while a socketed facet or Um still fits. That flexibility is why a top-rolled 2/20 can out-demand a Shako for a min-maxed caster.
items.teachingPoint: The shorthand "2/20" means +2 to that class's skills (a class-specific prefix like 'Arch-Angel's' for sorc) and 20% FCR (the suffix 'of the Magus'). It is NOT +2 to all skills. On a rare, +2 skills is a prefix and 20 FCR is a suffix, so a perfect one still has slots left for life, resists, strength and a socket.
factClaims: A rare circlet can roll +2 to a single class's skills (a class-specific magic prefix), not +2 to all skills
The 20% FCR suffix on circlets is 'of the Magus' and is the maximum single-affix FCR a circlet can roll
'2/20' shorthand means +2 class skills and 20% Faster Cast Rate
+2 skills is a prefix and 20 FCR is a suffix, so both can appear on the same rare item alongside other affixes
Rare items have up to 3 prefixes and 3 suffixes
items.quality: Perfect roll adds +2 socket (circlet/coronet max 2 sockets), 20 FCR, life, and all-resist

items.name: Circlet vs Coronet vs Tiara vs Diadem (why the base decides the value)
items.rarityTier: Tiara/Diadem bases are the prized rare-circlet bases because of socket count
items.whyValuable: Same affixes, different ceiling. Circlet and Coronet cap at 2 sockets; Tiara and Diadem can roll 3 sockets. A 2/20 caster helm with 3 open sockets (only possible on Tiara/Diadem) is dramatically rarer and lets you slot three facets/jewels. Higher magic level on the elite bases also lets better affixes spawn and lets high rolls appear at lower character level.
items.teachingPoint: Traders say 'circlet' loosely, but the base matters. Circlet is normal, Coronet is exceptional, Tiara and Diadem are elite. Only Tiara and Diadem reach 3 sockets. You can only gamble up to Coronet; Tiara and Diadem come from drops, not the gambling screen.
factClaims: Circlet is the normal base, Coronet is exceptional, Tiara and Diadem are elite bases
Circlet and Coronet have a maximum of 2 sockets; Tiara and Diadem can have up to 3 sockets
Coronet required level is 39, quality level 52, magic level 8
Tiara quality level is 70 and magic level is 13
Diadem required level is 52, quality level 70, magic level 13, max sockets 3
Higher magic level lets higher-level affixes spawn and lets strong affixes appear at a lower character level
The gambling screen only offers Circlet and Coronet, not Tiara or Diadem

items.name: Magic +3 Skill-Tab Circlet of the Magus ("3/20 caster circlet")
items.alias: "3/20", e.g. "Volcanic Circlet of the Magus" (+3 Fire, 20 FCR)
items.rarityTier: Very rare; a magic-only roll that a rare item literally cannot produce
items.whyValuable: A magic item can carry exactly one prefix and one suffix, and the +3-to-a-skill-tree prefix (e.g. 'Volcanic' for +3 Fire skills) is a magic-only affix. So a magic circlet can hit +3 to a whole skill tree AND 20 FCR, which is a bigger single-tree skill boost than any rare circlet (+2 class max) or Shako. A fireball sorc or nova necro prizes the +3 to the exact tree over +2 to everything.
items.teachingPoint: This is why 'is it 2/20 or 3/20?' matters. A rare tops out at +2 to the whole class. A magic circlet can hit +3 but only to ONE skill tree, and only as a magic item (no life/resist/socket alongside it beyond the single suffix). '3/20' on a caster circlet almost always means a magic item.
factClaims: +3 to a single skill tree (e.g. +3 Fire Skills) is a magic prefix such as 'Volcanic'
A magic item can have only one prefix and one suffix
A magic circlet can therefore carry +3 to a skill tree and 20 FCR ('of the Magus') simultaneously but nothing else
A rare circlet cannot roll +3 to a skill tree; its skill affix maxes at +2 to a class
items.quality: Best when it also rolls 2 open sockets on the base

items.name: Rare Dual-Leech FCR Ring (life leech + mana leech + 10% FCR)
items.rarityTier: Very rare to hit all the right affixes together on a ring
items.whyValuable: A ring can only roll 10% FCR (there is no 20 FCR ring affix), so the 'godly' ring stacks that 10 FCR with life leech, mana leech, a resist, life and attack rating. That combination beats a Stone of Jordan or Bul-Kathos for hybrid/attack builds that want leech and cast rate in one slot, something no unique ring offers together.
items.teachingPoint: 10% FCR is the hard ceiling for a ring. Anyone advertising a '20 FCR ring' is mistaken or scamming; 20 FCR belongs to circlets, helms and crafted amulets, not rings. The value on a rare ring is how many good affixes stack on top of that 10 FCR.
factClaims: Rings can roll a maximum of 10% Faster Cast Rate
There is no ring affix that grants 20% FCR
Life leech and mana leech (dual leech) can both appear on the same rare ring
'of the Magus' (20 FCR) does not spawn on rings
items.quality: Perfect: 10 FCR, max life/mana leech, tri-res or dual-res, +life

items.name: Rare +2 Class-Skill / 10% FCR Amulet
items.rarityTier: Rare to hit +2 skills together with FCR and resists
items.whyValuable: Amulets can roll +2 to a class or +1 to all skills, but a RARE amulet's FCR caps at 10%. Stacking +2 class skills, 10 FCR, life, and dual/tri resist gives a caster resists that Mara's has and skills Mara's has, but tuned to the exact tree and with FCR Mara's lacks. It is the poor-man's answer that occasionally beats Mara's when you need that 10 FCR.
items.teachingPoint: The key ceiling: a RARE amulet maxes at 10% FCR. To get 20 FCR on an amulet you must CRAFT a Caster Amulet (10% base FCR affix plus a rolled 'of the Apprentice' 5-10%). This is exactly why crafted caster amulets can beat rare ones.
factClaims: A rare amulet's FCR maxes at 10%
A crafted Caster Amulet can reach 20% FCR by combining the guaranteed FCR with a rolled bonus
Amulets can roll +2 to a single class's skills
Crafted items can have their fixed mods plus up to 4 random affixes, more total mods than a rare
items.quality: Perfect: +2 class, 10 FCR, dual/tri res, +life

items.name: Crafted Caster Amulet (+2 skills / 20% FCR / life / res)
items.alias: "godly caster ammy", the amulet that beats the rare
items.rarityTier: Astronomically rare to hit the perfect roll; thousands of crafts without a 2/20
items.whyValuable: The Caster Amulet recipe guarantees Regenerate Mana, +Mana and FCR, then rolls up to four more random affixes. That guaranteed FCR can climb to 20% and stack with +2 class skills, life and resists, giving up to seven mods. A perfect one is the single best caster amulet in the game and openly beats Mara's for a min-maxer who wants the FCR breakpoint.
items.teachingPoint: This is the standout case where a crafted item beats both the best rare and a top unique. A crafted amulet can carry its three fixed mods plus four random affixes (seven total), more than a rare's six. Crafters report making thousands and never hitting the +2/20 combination.
factClaims: The Caster Amulet craft guarantees Regenerate Mana, +Mana, and Faster Cast Rate as fixed mods
A crafted item can carry its fixed mods plus up to 4 random affixes
A crafted Caster Amulet can reach 20% FCR while a rare amulet cannot
Caster crafts use magic amulet bases that can carry +2 class skills
items.quality: +2 class, 20 FCR, +life, resists

items.name: Rare 2/20 Bowazon Gloves (+2 Bow & Crossbow / 20% IAS)
items.rarityTier: Rare; the least demanded of the 2/20 glove types but strong when stacked
items.whyValuable: Gloves are one of the few slots that can carry +2 to the Amazon Bow & Crossbow skill tree AND 20% IAS. No unique glove gives both a bow-skill bonus and 20 IAS, so a rare or magic pair is genuinely best-in-slot for a bowazon chasing an attack-speed breakpoint, especially with dex, strength and resists added.
items.teachingPoint: Same 2/20 vs 3/20 rule as circlets. A RARE glove tops at +2 to the tree; a MAGIC glove can hit +3 to the bow tree ('3/20 bow gloves') but then only one suffix. The bow variant is the cheapest of the 2/20 gloves because fewer builds use it than caster or melee versions.
factClaims: Gloves can roll +2 to the Amazon Bow and Crossbow skill tree
Gloves can roll 20% Increased Attack Speed
A magic glove can reach +3 to a skill tree while a rare glove maxes at +2
The 2/20 bow glove is considered the least popular of the 2/20 glove types
items.quality: +2 bow, 20 IAS, +dex, +str, resists

items.name: Rare Dual-Leech 20 IAS Gloves (melee)
items.rarityTier: Rare to hit 20 IAS plus both leeches plus crushing blow together
items.whyValuable: For a melee build these stack 20% IAS, life leech, mana leech and crushing blow in one slot. That is more than Laying of Hands (which gives 20 IAS and demon damage but no leech) or Dracul's for builds that want raw leech plus speed. Value is polarizing: many argue leech belongs on rings, so these only shine when the whole affix set lands.
items.teachingPoint: Crushing blow on gloves caps at 5% (a small-but-real melee multiplier). The trap here is that leech on gloves is often called low-value because players get leech from rings, so a dual-leech glove only commands a premium when it also carries 20 IAS and crushing blow or resists.
factClaims: Gloves can roll 20% IAS, life leech, mana leech, and crushing blow
Crushing blow on gloves maxes at 5%
Laying of Hands provides 20% IAS and bonus damage to demons but no leech
items.quality: 20 IAS, max dual leech, 5 CB, resists

items.name: Rare Boots: 30% FRW / 10% FHR / Tri-Res / +Dex
items.rarityTier: Very rare to hit FRW and FHR together with three resists
items.whyValuable: Uniques force a trade-off: Sandstorm Trek gives FHR but not much run speed, War Traveler gives MF and damage, Waterwalk gives life. No unique boot gives 30 FRW + 10 FHR + three resists at once. A rare that hits all of them is best-in-slot for casters and tanks who want mobility, a hit-recovery breakpoint and capped resists from the feet.
items.teachingPoint: The rare combination is FRW and FHR together, since both are suffixes-adjacent competitors for slots and rarely coexist. A pair with three resists, 30 FRW and 10 FHR (plus dex or MF) is the ceiling and commonly commands a high rune. Boots' resists let you free up other slots.
factClaims: Rare boots can roll 30% Faster Run/Walk, 10% Faster Hit Recovery, and three resistances together
Sandstorm Trek provides Faster Hit Recovery but not high Faster Run/Walk
War Traveler is favored for magic find and adds melee damage
The FRW + FHR combination on boots is uncommon, raising value
items.quality: 30 FRW, 10 FHR, tri-res, +dex or MF

items.name: Rare Jewel: 40% ED / 15% IAS ("40/15 jewel")
items.rarityTier: Very rare at max roll; a benchmark socket-filler
items.whyValuable: A single jewel giving 40% enhanced damage and 15% IAS is the strongest general damage-plus-speed socket filler for physical builds. It competes directly with an Ohm rune: 40/15 adds more if the weapon's base damage is under 75, Ohm adds more above that. Off-weapon it's an easy IAS+damage source for armor and helms. Perfect ones sell for multiple high runes.
items.teachingPoint: '40/15' or '15/40' is a jewel and the numbers are % Enhanced Damage and % IAS. The magic version is a 'Ruby Jewel of Fervor'; a rare can add resists or other stats on top. The 40 ED must be exact to be 'perfect' since the affix rolls a range.
factClaims: A jewel can roll a maximum of 40% Enhanced Damage and 15% IAS
The magic name for a 40/15 jewel is a 'Ruby Jewel of Fervor'
A 40/15 jewel adds more damage than an Ohm rune when the weapon base damage is below 75, and less above 75
Jewels can be socketed into weapons, armor, helms and shields
items.quality: Exactly 40 ED / 15 IAS; rare version adds resist

items.name: Rare LLD FCR Ring (level-30 bracket: 10 FCR / mana / life / dual res)
items.rarityTier: Niche but fiercely demanded inside the LLD bracket
items.whyValuable: In the level-30 dueling bracket, uniques are locked out by level requirements, so a rare ring with 10 FCR, mana, life, FHR-adjacent stats and dual resist at a low required level is best-in-slot. A perfect low-requirement Nagelring or a clean rare with 75 AR is worth more to an LLD player than most endgame unique rings, because the bracket is all about maxing every affix slot under a level cap.
items.teachingPoint: LLD value is inverted from PvM: required level is a stat. A rare ring that rolls its affixes at, say, level 25-30 instead of 40+ is far more valuable, because the whole point is packing max stats under a level cap. Casters at clvl 30 want 20 FCR from gear, and rings supply 10 of it.
factClaims: Rings max at 10% FCR, so LLD casters get 10 FCR per ring toward their breakpoint
Unique rings are gated by required level, restricting them in low-level brackets
A perfect Nagelring with 75% attack rating can be worth more to an LLD player than most unique rings
Lower affix required level increases an item's LLD value
items.quality: Low req level, 10 FCR, +life, +mana, dual res

items.name: Rare 2/20 Trap Assassin Circlet (+2 Assassin / 20% FCR / FRW)
items.alias: "2/20 sin circ", "Witch-Hunter's Circlet of the Magus"
items.rarityTier: Very rare; the ideal trapper head roll
items.whyValuable: Trap assassins want a specific FCR breakpoint for laying traps and casting. A rare circlet giving +2 Assassin skills, 20 FCR, faster run/walk, resists and a socket is the acknowledged best-in-slot trapper head, ahead of Griffon's or Nightwing's for trappers because those give no skills-to-class and no FCR tuned to the build.
items.teachingPoint: The +2 Assassin prefix on a circlet is named 'Witch-Hunter's'. Because trappers care about FCR and mobility, the ideal is +2 sin / 20 FCR / +FRW / resist, a combination only a rare (or a class-skill magic + magus) circlet can assemble.
factClaims: A rare circlet can roll +2 to Assassin skills (the 'Witch-Hunter's' prefix)
The 20% FCR suffix on the circlet is 'of the Magus'
Trap assassins target FCR breakpoints, making a 2/20 sin circlet best-in-slot for the build
Circlets can also roll Faster Run/Walk and resistances
items.quality: +2 sin, 20 FCR, +FRW, resist, socket

found.notes:
Research is READ-ONLY; no files created or modified. Economy framing is mature D2R ladder; tiers are openly guesses, no prices given.

CRITICAL FACT SPINE verified across multiple sources and worth double-checking before publishing each item:
1. FCR ceilings by slot: RARE amulet = 10 FCR max; RING = 10 FCR max (no 20 FCR ring exists); CIRCLET/HELM = 20 FCR via 'of the Magus' suffix; CRAFTED caster amulet = 20 FCR (10 base + rolled apprentice bonus). This distinction drives most of the 'rare beats unique' logic. Confirmed via purediablo, diablo2.io, d2jsp.
2. Skill affix ceilings: RARE circlet/glove/amulet = +2 to ONE class (class-specific magic prefix, e.g. Arch-Angel's/Witch-Hunter's). MAGIC item = +3 to ONE skill TREE (e.g. 'Volcanic' +3 fire). Neither rare nor magic circlet can roll +2 ALL skills — that is unique (Shako) only. This is the core of the 2/20 vs 3/20 shorthand. Well-confirmed.
3. Base tiers: Circlet(normal)/Coronet(exc, rlvl39, mlvl8)/Tiara(elite, qlvl70, mlvl13)/Diadem(elite, rlvl52, qlvl70, mlvl13). Circlet+Coronet cap 2 sockets; Tiara+Diadem cap 3 sockets. Gambling only offers Circlet+Coronet. Source: diablo.fandom Coronet page + diablo2.io forums. RECOMMEND cross-checking exact Coronet rlvl (39) and socket caps against Arreat Summit / diablo2.io base pages before publishing — diablo2.io and diablowiki both returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch, so base-stat numbers come from search-snippet summaries, not the primary page. Treat rlvl/qlvl/mlvl numbers as needing one more primary-source pass.
4. Jewel 40/15 = max ED 40% + max IAS 15%; magic name 'Ruby Jewel of Fervor'; Ohm-rune comparison threshold is weapon base dmg 75. Confirmed.
5. Crushing blow on gloves caps at 5%. Stated in trade listings; recommend confirming against affix table.

Sources leaned on: diablo2.io price-check threads, blizzard D2R forums, purediablo forums, d2jsp, itemforge/itemnow listings (for confirming which rolls exist as products), diablo2.diablowiki LLD guide. diablo2.io base pages and diablowiki article pages returned 403 to automated fetch — all diablo2.io info here is from search-result summaries. No single fully-authoritative base-stat table (Arreat Summit) was directly fetched; flag the numeric base stats for a human verify pass.

checked.name: Circlet vs Coronet vs Tiara vs Diadem base mechanics

checked.name: Magic +3 Skill-Tab Circlet of the Magus (3/20)

checked.name: Rare Dual-Leech FCR Ring (LL + ML + 10% FCR)

checked.name: Rare +2 Class-Skill / 10% FCR Amulet

checked.name: Crafted Caster Amulet (+2 skills / 20 FCR)

checked.name: Rare Boots 30 FRW / 10 FHR / Tri-Res / +Dex
checked.corrections: Verified. Max FRW on rare boots is 30%, max FHR is 10%; tri-res plus those together is confirmed (real listings). Sandstorm Trek gives FHR but low FRW; War Traveler favored for MF and adds melee damage. All correct.

checked.name: Rare/Magic Jewel 40% ED / 15% IAS (40/15)
checked.corrections: Verified. Max is 40% ED / 15% IAS. IMPORTANT: the perfect 40/15 is a MAGIC jewel - 'of Fervor' (15 IAS) does NOT spawn on rare jewels, so labeling it 'Rare/Magic' is loose; it should be described as magic. checked.name: Rare LLD FCR Ring (level-30 bracket)
checked.corrections: Core mechanics correct: rings cap at 10% FCR; unique rings are gated by required level; lower affix required-level raises LLD value.
